inheritanceRule: Every omitted field inherits the resolved parent class value.

profiles.name: Oozemorph

constraints.summary: The natural form is an amorphous ooze; humanoid form lasts limited hours and restricts equipment use.

evidence.reason: Compression, ooze immunities and scaling damage reduction reinforce survival.

profiles.playerSummary: An amorphous Shifter who mimics humanoid form for limited periods and develops fluid limbs, compression and ooze resilience.
profiles.tradeoff: Its true body cannot use normal equipment or communicate conventionally, creating major exploration and social complications.

profiles.name: Weretouched

constraints.summary: One lycanthropic animal aspect is selected permanently.

evidence.reason: A stable hybrid form gains lycanthropic resilience while retaining equipment and speech.

profiles.playerSummary: A Shifter committed to one lycanthropic hybrid form that preserves gear, speech and a humanoid silhouette.
profiles.tradeoff: Broad animal-form flexibility is exchanged for one permanent thematic and mechanical form choice.

profiles.name: Court Poet
profiles.sourceCitationText: Heroes of the High Court pg. 6

evidence.reason: The performance enhances mental and social ability rather than physical rage.

profiles.playerSummary: A courtly Skald whose performance heightens intellect and charisma instead of driving allies into physical rage.
profiles.tradeoff: The class’s direct martial boost is reduced, favouring casters and social or intellectual parties.

profiles.name: Spell Warrior

evidence.reason: Multiple features are devoted to countering, weakening and manipulating enemy spells.

profiles.playerSummary: A Skald who enchants allied weapons through song while countering and tampering with enemy spellcasting.
profiles.tradeoff: Several personal rage powers and performance benefits are redirected into weapons and reactive magic.

profiles.name: Crossblooded

constraints.summary: Two bloodlines are chosen; their arcana combine but powers and spells must be selected between them.

evidence.reason: Two bloodline identities are combined at the price of reduced spells known and weaker mental saves.

profiles.playerSummary: A Sorcerer combining two bloodlines, mixing their arcana and choosing powers and spells from either lineage.
profiles.tradeoff: One fewer spell known at every level and a Will-save penalty make the hybrid substantially less forgiving.

profiles.name: Razmiran Priest

constraints.summary: Razmiran priesthood is a narrative identity, not a hard deity or institutional gate imposed by the engine.

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The archetype explicitly impersonates divine authority and performs a priestly role through arcane deception.

evidence.reason: Cleric spell access and divine-item activation add strong healing without true divine casting.

profiles.playerSummary: An arcane impostor who convincingly performs priesthood and accesses divine healing through spell knowledge and magic items.
profiles.tradeoff: The divine identity is deliberately false, and much of the strongest flexibility depends on consumable magic items.

profiles.name: Phantom Blade

constraints.summary: The phantom manifests as one bonded weapon rather than an independent companion.

evidence.reason: The independent phantom is replaced by a weapon used through spell combat and spellstrike.

profiles.playerSummary: A Spiritualist whose phantom becomes a bonded weapon, creating a spell-combat martial hybrid instead of a two-creature team.
profiles.tradeoff: The independent phantom and its separate actions disappear, and the character becomes weapon dependent.

profiles.name: Priest of the Fallen

professionIdentity.evidenceText: The source explicitly presents a priest who invokes fallen hero-gods and channels their divine energy.

evidence.reason: Six hero-god archetypes let the manifested phantom support, cast, fight or lead in distinct ways.
A positive-channel version can damage undead, depending on alignment and the permanent energy choice.

profiles.playerSummary: A priest who calls one of several fallen hero-god phantoms and channels its legendary role and divine energy.
profiles.tradeoff: Only one hero-god can be channelled each day, and it refuses confinement inside the Spiritualist for most of the career.

profiles.name: Master Summoner

evidence.section: Summoning Mastery / Hordes of Summoned Monsters
evidence.reason: The archetype sustains multiple summon-monster effects and gains Augment Summoning.

profiles.playerSummary: A Summoner who weakens the eidolon to maintain multiple enhanced summoned creatures at once.
profiles.tradeoff: It creates one of the game’s heaviest multi-creature workloads and leaves the permanent eidolon significantly weaker.

profiles.name: Synthesist

evidence.reason: The eidolon is worn as a living form that supplies physical abilities, evolutions and temporary hit points.

profiles.playerSummary: A Summoner who fuses with the eidolon as living armour, personally using its body, evolutions and natural attacks.
profiles.tradeoff: The separate companion and its action economy are lost except for a late limited split-forms ability.
